summary.oneLiner: Hikal is a turnaround/normalization story. After ~3 years of flat-to-declining top line (FY24–FY26), management frames FY26 as the trough and a "transition year," with FY27 expected to be "stronger and more positive." The two drags: (a) a US FDA warning letter on the Bangalore pharma site (~9 months old at call date) which slowed pharma shipments and muted CDMO/NCE growth; (b) a multi-year global agrochem inventory/pricing downcycle, now described as "largely behind us." Recovery levers: improving demand across API + CDMO, new strategic assets going operational (HPAPI lab, Pune R&D/Kilo lab, Panoli pilot plant), China+1 RFP momentum, and an Animal Health ramp targeting INR500cr+ in 4–5 years. Key risk gating the thesis: US FDA resolution, hoped "by end of this year," which historically takes 18–24 months.

scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | FY26 | YoY / Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (consol) | INR 519 cr | INR 1,713 cr | FY26 degrew YoY (FY25 was flat); 3-yr CAGR < mid-single-digit |
| EBITDA | INR 105 cr | INR 220 cr | — |
| EBITDA margin | 20.3% | 12.9% | Q4 margin improved QoQ; product-mix driven |
| PAT (reported) | INR 14.4 cr | PBT negative INR 79.3 cr | After exceptional items |
| PBT (normalized) | — | ~INR 7 cr | Adjusting FY26 exceptional of INR 85 cr |
| Net debt / leverage | — | D/E 0.56 (from 0.59) | Modest deleveraging YoY (as on 31-Mar-2026) |
| Capex (FY26) | — | INR 149 cr | Debottlenecking, regulatory upgrades, CDMO capacity |

**Segment splits:**
- Pharma: Q4 rev INR 292 cr, EBIT INR 35 cr (12.0% margin); FY26 rev INR 1,021 cr, EBIT INR 58 cr (5.7%). Q4 operating profit +45% QoQ on flat revenue.
- Crop Protection: Q4 rev INR 228 cr, EBIT INR 39 cr (17.1%); FY26 rev INR 692 cr, EBIT INR 58 cr (8.4%).

**One-offs (explicit):**
- Q4 FY26: exceptional INR 47 cr impairment of part of Panoli manufacturing plant (multipurpose agrochem facility being retooled to pharma).
- FY26 full year: exceptional INR 85 cr total — comprising the impairment charges + a charge on account of the new labour code. Adjusted PBT would have been ~INR 7 cr (vs reported PBT of −INR 79.3 cr).
guidance (critical):
- **No formal FY27 numeric guidance given** — management repeatedly declined, citing war/raw-material/logistics uncertainty; promised guidance at Q1 FY27 call.
- **Directional:** FY27 to be "stronger and more positive than FY26"; positive volume growth in BOTH pharma and crop; "growth will come back" (toward FY23/FY24 levels) contingent on FY27. Q1 FY27 is seasonally lowest (annual maintenance shutdowns) and may see marginal margin pressure from RM cost lag.
- **Pharma vs Crop growth mix:** Future growth to be led by CDMO/Pharma, Animal Health and Specialty Chemicals; Crop will show "some growth" but is the laggard driver.
- **Margins:** FY27 margins expected to "sustain at improved levels" (operating leverage, mix, business-excellence).
- **New molecules / DMF filings:** Targeting **5–6 DMF filings annually** (up from 2–3 historically), pharma-only; Animal Health filings on top of that. New filings now done from Panoli site (FDA-approved, no warning) to de-risk from Bangalore.
- **Product launches:** Key launches planned in Japan & Brazil over FY27–FY28; setting up Brazil office; engaging South Korea.
- **Capex:** Impaired multipurpose asset to be retooled (INR ~250 cr of the original INR 300 cr build redeployed into new pharma + animal-health lines), generating revenue "in the year to come"; HPAPI manufacturing facility in Pune targeted ~FY28.
- **Long-term:** FY30 plan (~INR 3,500–4,000 cr medium-term, INR 6,000 cr FY30 target referenced by analysts) "still stands" but delayed ~2–3 years.
pipeline (cdmo / molecules):
- DMF filings ramping to 5–6/yr; pipeline shifting to differentiated/specialty.
- CDMO: healthy increase in RFP activity; several programs advancing from early-stage to scale-up; China+1 driving innovators to India.
- Complex therapeutic focus: oncology, CNS, gastroenterology, antidiabetics.
- **HPAPI / ADC:** lab work just started; moving from mature OEB2/OEB3 toward high-potent OEB4/OEB5 (anticancer). ADC scope = payload + linker synthesis only (NOT biologics). Long-term: 3–5 years to meaningful revenue; HPAPI mfg facility targeted FY28.
- Crop: NCE products already commercialized; new NCEs won/validated last year to launch next FY (pilot trials ongoing); deeper contract-mfg + co-development + long-term supply agreements with global innovators (a few onboarded in FY26).
- Animal Health: completed validation of all products under global MNC contract, moving to commercial phase; encouraging RFPs (innovator + niche).
segment view:
- **Pharma (FY26 INR 1,021 cr, 5.7% EBIT):** H1 soft (FDA-driven slowdown — GMP consultants advised "pressure testing"/going slow on Bangalore production); H2 recovery. Panoli + Bangalore pharma plants at ~80–85% utilization (utilization optically up partly due to longer batch cycle times post-CAPA). API demand "encouraging" across regulated + emerging markets. CDMO is the segment hit by FDA (new NCE growth muted; existing business intact); Panoli (FDA-approved May 2023) offers FDA-clean CDMO capacity.
- **Crop Protection (FY26 INR 692 cr, 8.4% EBIT):** Q4 strong recovery (rev INR 228 cr, 17.1% margin) on volume offtake + value-chain normalization. Inventory correction "more or less done"; true demand back BUT pricing pressure persists (China has NOT raised agrochem prices). Mix shift to NCEs, contract mfg, long-term supply.
- **Animal Health:** steady traction; on track for INR 500 cr+ business in 4–5 years (~INR 100–150 cr starting FY27, per prior September guidance — management confirmed "on track" but declined fresh FY27 number). No customer indications of degrowth despite Zoetis/BI flagging degrowth on their calls. Moving toward higher-complexity, lower-competition, higher-margin products. NOT into steroids/reproductive hormones (requires different facility; website info "outdated").
growth / optionality:
- **China+1 / CDMO:** core structural tailwind; innovators diversifying away from single-source (China) geographies — explicit beneficiary positioning for both pharma and animal health.
- New assets now live: HPAPI lab + expanded Pune R&D + Pune Kilo lab (end-to-end CDMO incl. clinical trial material from one location) + Panoli pilot plant (US FDA-approved).
- Geographic: Japan (strong engagement), Brazil (office being set up), South Korea (new BD).
- Specialty Chemicals & Personal Care: leveraging existing crop tech/assets for adjacent high-value segments.
- Impaired Panoli asset retooled → new pharma + animal-health lines (revenue upside FY27+).
margins & cost:
- Q4 EBITDA margin 20.3% (improved QoQ); FY26 12.9%. Pharma Q4 EBIT margin 12% (op profit +45% QoQ); Crop Q4 17.1%.
- Margin levers: better product mix, higher utilization, operating leverage, backward integration, business-excellence framework.
- **RM cost headwind (explicit):** solvent prices (toluene, methanol, acetone, benzene/BTX) "shot up" in last 3 months due to war; normalized but at much higher levels; availability OK (was tight in March). CDMO has pass-through with ~1-quarter lag (negotiations ongoing); own/old products competitive but increases being pursued. Net effect: marginal hit possible in Q1 FY27, no significant bottom-line impact expected over the year.
- China not raising RM/KSM prices (govt absorbing via subsidies) — keeps Indian players cost-disadvantaged short-term.
capex:
- FY26 capex INR 149 cr (debottlenecking, regulatory upgrades, CDMO capacity).
- ~INR 900 cr capex over FY22–FY26: ~INR 600 cr growth + ~INR 300 cr infra/regulatory/maintenance. Of the INR 600 cr growth, INR 300 cr went into the multipurpose asset now being partly impaired (INR 47 cr impaired; ~INR 250 cr retooled to new pharma/animal-health lines). The other INR 300 cr growth capex "has already grown" (incl. Panoli pharma + animal-health multipurpose plant under MNC contract).
- HPAPI manufacturing facility (Pune) targeted FY28.
capital allocation / deleveraging:
- D/E reduced to 0.56 from 0.59 (as on 31-Mar-2026) — modest.
- Growth funded by mix of internal accruals + debt; capital allocation described as "highly targeted / high-ROI."
- ROCE acknowledged as depressed (was historically 15–18%); target to return to 18–20%+. No buyback/dividend discussion.
risks:
- **US FDA (Bangalore site):** warning letter ~9 months old; gates CDMO/NCE growth; resolution "hoped" by end of FY27 but historically 18–24 months; FDA gives no confirmation — "they just show up" for inspection. Inspection expected toward end of this year.
- **Agro cyclicality / pricing:** demand recovering but pricing pressure persists; China not raising prices.
- **RM / geopolitical:** war-driven solvent inflation; pass-through lag; Q1 FY27 margin risk.
- **Track record / execution credibility:** repeated analyst pushback on 3 lost years, underperformance vs peer pharma-CDMO players, ~INR 900–1,000 cr capex with little top-line to show, FY30 targets repeatedly delayed.
- **Leverage:** still ~0.56 D/E with negative reported PBT in FY26.
- **Animal Health customer concentration:** dependence on a global MNC contract; Zoetis/BI flagging degrowth in segment.
management tone: Measured, defensive-but-confident. Repeatedly acknowledged "lost 2–3 years," "aberration," "worst is behind us." Notably guidance-shy — declined every numeric FY27 ask, deferring to Q1 FY27 call (citing war uncertainty). Emphasized compliance/quality investment and "future-proofing" the system. Faced pointed, skeptical analyst questioning on wealth creation, capital efficiency and management capability (which MD rejected).
non-obvious points:
- Utilization (80–85%) optically inflated by longer batch cycle times from added post-CAPA QC checks — i.e., not purely demand-driven.
- The impaired plant is an agrochem multipurpose facility being CONVERTED to pharma — capital reallocation across divisions, not pure write-off.
- New DMF filings deliberately shifted to Panoli (FDA-clean) to de-risk from the Bangalore warning-letter site — implicit admission Bangalore approvals are stalled for the year.
- NCE volumes being split across multiple qualified suppliers while FDA pending → growth muted even on existing NCE wins.
- Pollution-control board issue (prior overhang) settled in court, attributed to an external transporter, "nothing to do with Hikal manufacturing."
- Mgmt corrected analyst's outdated website info: Hikal is NOT in steroids/reproductive hormones (needs different facility).
challenges → beneficiaries:
- China+1 / supply-chain diversification away from single-source China → benefits Indian API/CDMO/Animal-Health players including Hikal (and broader Indian CRAMS peers). ⭐
- China agrochem/petchem capacity rationalization (Ministry of Agriculture shutting old/toxic plants; old petchem to close by 2029, export quotas) → potential medium-term pricing/order tailwind for ex-China agrochem suppliers (not yet visible in pricing per mgmt). ⭐
- Rising oncology/HPAPI/ADC share of new FDA approvals → opportunity for HPAPI-capable CDMOs (Hikal entering, 3–5 yr horizon).

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Vision stated as "To be the leading global fine chemical company to the Pharmaceutical, Crop Protection, and Specialty Chemical Industries"; mission is to "create value through superior, chemical products and operate as a responsible company".
- Described as "Hikal's 38-year journey of capability building", founded 1988 by Jai Hiremath, with milestones including the first plant at Mahad (1991), Taloja commissioned in 1997 "for a US innovator CDMO project", and the Novartis manufacturing site acquired at Panoli, Gujarat in 2000.
- "Serving clients across five regions worldwide - powered by six manufacturing & R&D sites in India": 5 regions served, 4 global office hubs, 6 manufacturing & R&D sites, 3 Indian states present (India, Europe, Japan, USA named as office geographies).
- Pharma is "Strengthened presence across regulated and emerging markets with increasing focus on Japan, LATAM, MENA and other strategic geographies"; the deck cites "100+ customer audits passed at Bangalore facility".
- Long-standing CDMO relationships evidenced by a 2021 milestone: "Signed a 10-year multiproduct contract with a leading global animal health innovator".

segment_detail.title: Segment view
segment_detail.body:
- **Pharma (FY26 INR 1,021 cr, 5.7% EBIT):** H1 soft (FDA-driven slowdown — GMP consultants advised "pressure testing"/going slow on Bangalore production); H2 recovery. Panoli + Bangalore pharma plants at ~80–85% utilization (utilization optically up partly due to longer batch cycle times post-CAPA). API demand "encouraging" across regulated + emerging markets. CDMO is the segment hit by FDA (new NCE growth muted; existing business intact); Panoli (FDA-approved May 2023) offers FDA-clean CDMO capacity.
- **Crop Protection (FY26 INR 692 cr, 8.4% EBIT):** Q4 strong recovery (rev INR 228 cr, 17.1% margin) on volume offtake + value-chain normalization. Inventory correction "more or less done"; true demand back BUT pricing pressure persists (China has NOT raised agrochem prices). Mix shift to NCEs, contract mfg, long-term supply.
- **Animal Health:** steady traction; on track for INR 500 cr+ business in 4–5 years (~INR 100–150 cr starting FY27, per prior September guidance — management confirmed "on track" but declined fresh FY27 number). No customer indications of degrowth despite Zoetis/BI flagging degrowth on their calls. Moving toward higher-complexity, lower-competition, higher-margin products. NOT into steroids/reproductive hormones (requires different facility; website info "outdated").

order_book.title: Pipeline (CDMO / molecules)
order_book.body:
- DMF filings ramping to 5–6/yr; pipeline shifting to differentiated/specialty.
- CDMO: healthy increase in RFP activity; several programs advancing from early-stage to scale-up; China+1 driving innovators to India.
- Complex therapeutic focus: oncology, CNS, gastroenterology, antidiabetics.
- **HPAPI / ADC:** lab work just started; moving from mature OEB2/OEB3 toward high-potent OEB4/OEB5 (anticancer). ADC scope = payload + linker synthesis only (NOT biologics). Long-term: 3–5 years to meaningful revenue; HPAPI mfg facility targeted FY28.
- Crop: NCE products already commercialized; new NCEs won/validated last year to launch next FY (pilot trials ongoing); deeper contract-mfg + co-development + long-term supply agreements with global innovators (a few onboarded in FY26).
- Animal Health: completed validation of all products under global MNC contract, moving to commercial phase; encouraging RFPs (innovator + niche).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)
guidance.body:
- **No formal FY27 numeric guidance given** — management repeatedly declined, citing war/raw-material/logistics uncertainty; promised guidance at Q1 FY27 call.
- **Directional:** FY27 to be "stronger and more positive than FY26"; positive volume growth in BOTH pharma and crop; "growth will come back" (toward FY23/FY24 levels) contingent on FY27. Q1 FY27 is seasonally lowest (annual maintenance shutdowns) and may see marginal margin pressure from RM cost lag.
- **Pharma vs Crop growth mix:** Future growth to be led by CDMO/Pharma, Animal Health and Specialty Chemicals; Crop will show "some growth" but is the laggard driver.
- **Margins:** FY27 margins expected to "sustain at improved levels" (operating leverage, mix, business-excellence).
- **New molecules / DMF filings:** Targeting **5–6 DMF filings annually** (up from 2–3 historically), pharma-only; Animal Health filings on top of that. New filings now done from Panoli site (FDA-approved, no warning) to de-risk from Bangalore.
- **Product launches:** Key launches planned in Japan & Brazil over FY27–FY28; setting up Brazil office; engaging South Korea.
- **Capex:** Impaired multipurpose asset to be retooled (INR ~250 cr of the original INR 300 cr build redeployed into new pharma + animal-health lines), generating revenue "in the year to come"; HPAPI manufacturing facility in Pune targeted ~FY28.
- **Long-term:** FY30 plan (~INR 3,500–4,000 cr medium-term, INR 6,000 cr FY30 target referenced by analysts) "still stands" but delayed ~2–3 years.

growth_optionality.title: Growth / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **China+1 / CDMO:** core structural tailwind; innovators diversifying away from single-source (China) geographies — explicit beneficiary positioning for both pharma and animal health.
- New assets now live: HPAPI lab + expanded Pune R&D + Pune Kilo lab (end-to-end CDMO incl. clinical trial material from one location) + Panoli pilot plant (US FDA-approved).
- Geographic: Japan (strong engagement), Brazil (office being set up), South Korea (new BD).
- Specialty Chemicals & Personal Care: leveraging existing crop tech/assets for adjacent high-value segments.
- Impaired Panoli asset retooled → new pharma + animal-health lines (revenue upside FY27+).

margins.title: Margins & cost
margins.body:
- Q4 EBITDA margin 20.3% (improved QoQ); FY26 12.9%. Pharma Q4 EBIT margin 12% (op profit +45% QoQ); Crop Q4 17.1%.
- Margin levers: better product mix, higher utilization, operating leverage, backward integration, business-excellence framework.
- **RM cost headwind (explicit):** solvent prices (toluene, methanol, acetone, benzene/BTX) "shot up" in last 3 months due to war; normalized but at much higher levels; availability OK (was tight in March). CDMO has pass-through with ~1-quarter lag (negotiations ongoing); own/old products competitive but increases being pursued. Net effect: marginal hit possible in Q1 FY27, no significant bottom-line impact expected over the year.
- China not raising RM/KSM prices (govt absorbing via subsidies) — keeps Indian players cost-disadvantaged short-term.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation / deleveraging
capital_allocation.body:
- D/E reduced to 0.56 from 0.59 (as on 31-Mar-2026) — modest.
- Growth funded by mix of internal accruals + debt; capital allocation described as "highly targeted / high-ROI."
- ROCE acknowledged as depressed (was historically 15–18%); target to return to 18–20%+. No buyback/dividend discussion.

management_tone.title: Management tone
management_tone.body: Measured, defensive-but-confident. Repeatedly acknowledged "lost 2–3 years," "aberration," "worst is behind us." Notably guidance-shy — declined every numeric FY27 ask, deferring to Q1 FY27 call (citing war uncertainty). Emphasized compliance/quality investment and "future-proofing" the system. Faced pointed, skeptical analyst questioning on wealth creation, capital efficiency and management capability (which MD rejected).

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **US FDA (Bangalore site):** warning letter ~9 months old; gates CDMO/NCE growth; resolution "hoped" by end of FY27 but historically 18–24 months; FDA gives no confirmation — "they just show up" for inspection. Inspection expected toward end of this year.
- **Agro cyclicality / pricing:** demand recovering but pricing pressure persists; China not raising prices.
- **RM / geopolitical:** war-driven solvent inflation; pass-through lag; Q1 FY27 margin risk.
- **Track record / execution credibility:** repeated analyst pushback on 3 lost years, underperformance vs peer pharma-CDMO players, ~INR 900–1,000 cr capex with little top-line to show, FY30 targets repeatedly delayed.
- **Leverage:** still ~0.56 D/E with negative reported PBT in FY26.
- **Animal Health customer concentration:** dependence on a global MNC contract; Zoetis/BI flagging degrowth in segment.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious points
non_obvious.body:
- Utilization (80–85%) optically inflated by longer batch cycle times from added post-CAPA QC checks — i.e., not purely demand-driven.
- The impaired plant is an agrochem multipurpose facility being CONVERTED to pharma — capital reallocation across divisions, not pure write-off.
- New DMF filings deliberately shifted to Panoli (FDA-clean) to de-risk from the Bangalore warning-letter site — implicit admission Bangalore approvals are stalled for the year.
- NCE volumes being split across multiple qualified suppliers while FDA pending → growth muted even on existing NCE wins.
- Pollution-control board issue (prior overhang) settled in court, attributed to an external transporter, "nothing to do with Hikal manufacturing."
- Mgmt corrected analyst's outdated website info: Hikal is NOT in steroids/reproductive hormones (needs different facility).

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- China+1 / supply-chain diversification away from single-source China → benefits Indian API/CDMO/Animal-Health players including Hikal (and broader Indian CRAMS peers). ⭐
- China agrochem/petchem capacity rationalization (Ministry of Agriculture shutting old/toxic plants; old petchem to close by 2029, export quotas) → potential medium-term pricing/order tailwind for ex-China agrochem suppliers (not yet visible in pricing per mgmt). ⭐
- Rising oncology/HPAPI/ADC share of new FDA approvals → opportunity for HPAPI-capable CDMOs (Hikal entering, 3–5 yr horizon).

---

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Trough/transition year confirmed. Q4 sequential recovery in both segments (Pharma op profit +45% QoQ; Crop Q4 17.1% EBIT margin). INR 85 cr FY26 exceptional (INR 47 cr Panoli impairment + labour code). D/E 0.56 (from 0.59). FDA warning letter (~9 months) gating CDMO/NCE; resolution hoped end-FY27. NO FY27 guidance (deferred to Q1 FY27 call). DMF filings ramping to 5–6/yr (from Panoli). HPAPI/ADC (payload+linker) entered, FY28 mfg facility. Animal Health INR 500cr+ in 4–5 yrs reaffirmed. War-driven solvent inflation flagged as Q1 FY27 margin risk.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [US FDA remediation] "In our Pharmaceutical Business we are in the penultimate stage of our remediation plan with the US FDA. A significant amount of time and resources have been invested to ensure the highest level of compliance", with "Continued engagement with the US FDA, with reinspection expected during the current FY"; the deck frames the year as a transition "from regulatory-led disruption to growth".
- [Input cost / geopolitics] In Crop Protection, "geopolitical developments led to a significant rise across all input costs including raw materials, resulting in margin pressure", with management expecting "a sequential improvement going forward".
- [Labour code] A new labour/wage code drove an FY26 exceptional item of "Rs. 38 crores", with a Q1FY27 exceptional item that "relates to reversal of excess provision made during Q3FY26 for implementation of new labour code"; HR update notes "Salary restructuring as per the new wage code has been completed" and townhalls at all sites on "the New Wage Code and Impact".
- [Asset impairment] The FY26 exceptional items also include "Impairment (Rs. 47 crores) of manufacturing asset at Panoli".
- [CSR] Four programmes described - Kaushalya & Suraksha (healthcare and safety), Anahat (environment, including a partnership "with WWF India to advance its Nature Guardian conservation program"), Medha (education and skill development) and Rachana (heritage, art and culture).
